function.mechanism: Hydrates to form viscous, shear-thinning solutions that stabilize emulsions and suspensions and modify food texture.
common_food_categories: special medical purpose infant formula categories

adi.basis: EFSA 2017 re-evaluation concluded no need for a numerical ADI; 2023 follow-up found no safety concern for assessed infant FSMP use.

efsa.key_finding: No safety concern was identified at assessed uses; EFSA maintained no numerical ADI and concluded no safety concern for infants below 16 weeks in FC 13.1.5.1 under assessed exposure scenarios.

fda.notes: Listed as a direct food additive with defined conditions/specifications; not identified in searched Part 184 GRAS entries for xanthan gum.

adi.basis: WHO JECFA database entry for XANTHAN GUM (Chemical 802) lists ADI as NOT SPECIFIED.

concerns.summary: Case reports and surveillance-linked publications reported late-onset necrotizing enterocolitis in some premature infants exposed to xanthan-containing thickened feeds; evidence is signal-generating rather than definitive causality.
Recent mechanistic and model studies show xanthan gum can alter microbial composition/function; findings demonstrate biological activity but do not establish clear harm at approved dietary uses.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2017 reported no concern for genotoxicity and no adverse effects in chronic/carcinogenicity studies at highest tested doses.
EFSA 2017 and 2023 concluded no safety concern at assessed uses/exposure scenarios.
JECFA lists ADI as not specified and includes a no-safety-concern conclusion in assessed infant-formula context (2016 entry).

populations: Infants below 16 weeks consuming FSMP/special formulae
adi_exceedance.notes: Classical ADI exceedance is not applicable because EFSA/JECFA use a non-numerical ADI approach for xanthan gum.

risk_assessment.rationale: Current evidence supports broad regulatory acceptance with no numerical ADI and no confirmed major toxicological hazard at authorized uses. Remaining uncertainty is concentrated in very-young-infant contexts and microbiome modulation signals.
key_factors: US CFR approval with defined manufacturing/specification conditions
Infant NEC signal reports and microbiome-modulation findings warrant monitoring
